features.claim: Triceratops had a large bony frill.
features.quote: Bearing a large bony frill, three horns on the skull, and a large, four-legged body, exhibiting convergent evolution with rhinoceroses, Triceratops is one of the most recognizable of all dinosaurs and the best-known ceratopsian.

features.claim: Triceratops had three horns on its skull.

features.claim: Triceratops had a large, four-legged body.
features.quote: Bearing a large bony frill, three horns on the skull, and a large, four-legged body, exhibiting convergent evolution with rhinoceroses, Triceratops is one of the most recognizable of all dinosaurs and the best-known ceratopsian.

features.claim: Triceratops had a single horn on the snout above the nostrils.
features.quote: The skull bore a single horn on the snout above the nostrils.

features.claim: Triceratops had a pair of brow horns about 1 meter long, one above each eye.
features.quote: The skull also featured a pair of supraorbital "brow" horns approximately 1 meter (3.3 ft) long, with one above each eye.

features.claim: The front of the head had a large beak in front of its teeth.
features.quote: The front of the head was equipped with a large beak in front of its teeth.

features.claim: Triceratops had strong limbs, short hands with three hooves each, and short feet with four hooves each.
features.quote: Both Triceratops species possessed a very sturdy build, with strong limbs, short hands with three hooves each, and short feet with four hooves each.
Skin impressions have been found for Triceratops, showing that it had large, pebbled scales.

features.claim: Triceratops had a parrot-like beak and a large frill that could reach nearly one metre across.
features.quote: With its three horns, parrot-like beak and large frill that could reach nearly one metre across, the skull of Triceratops is one of the largest and most striking of any land animal.

features.claim: Triceratops had a large skull, among the largest of all land animals.
features.quote: The most distinctive feature is their large skull, among the largest of all land animals.

features.claim: Triceratops had a bony shield which covered its neck.
features.quote: Its defense had to stand up to attacks from taller theropods, hence the bony shield which covered its neck.

not_this.claim: Old pictures show Triceratops with its front legs sprawling out at angles, but it actually held an upright stance.
not_this.quote: Originally, it was believed that the front legs of the animal had to be sprawling at angles from the thorax, in order to better bear the weight of the head. This stance can be seen in paintings by Charles Knight and Rudolph Zallinger. However, evidence of trackways, and reconstructions of skeletons show that Triceratops and other ceratopsids had an upright stance during normal locomotion, with the elbows flexed and slightly bowed out.

second_reading.claim: Triceratops was not related to rhinoceroses, even though it looked a bit like one.
second_reading.quote: Triceratops wasn’t related to rhinoceroses at all.

second_reading.claim: Triceratops is often shown as a herding animal, but there is little evidence that they lived in herds.
second_reading.quote: Although Triceratops are commonly portrayed as herd animals, there is little evidence that they lived in herds.

second_reading.claim: Scientists disagree about whether Triceratops used its horns to fight each other with horns locked.
second_reading.quote: While studies show that such activity would be feasible, if unlike that of present-day horned animals, there is disagreement about whether they did so.

second_reading.claim: It is disputed whether Torosaurus is just a mature Triceratops.
second_reading.quote: This view has been highly disputed, with some morphometric research and the apparent existence of authentic Torosaurus subadults favoring the distinctness of the two genera, according to newer studies.

second_reading.claim: It is still possible that the differences between Triceratops skulls represent a single species with males and females looking different.
